## v2 has no online mode. Which command wipes the content synced into my browser?

--- [vault:corpus/docs/Migrate from v1.md] ---
### Removed features

# Removed features
Certain features have been removed:

* Online mode: v2 is sync mode only, meaning all your content will be synced into your browser. A simpler Online mode may be added back later. If you like to wipe your local content at any time, use the `System: Wipe Client` command.
* [Federation](https://v1.silverbullet.md/Federation)
* [Share](https://v1.silverbullet.md/Plugs/Share) replaced by [[^Library/Std/Infrastructure/Export]]
* Space Script: replaced by [[Space Lua]]
* Space Config: replaced by the [[API/config]] APIs.
* Command link syntax (`{[...]})`) replaced by the `${widgets.commandButton(...)}` API.

--- [vault:corpus/docs/PWA.md] ---
### What the PWA gives you

# What the PWA gives you
* **Offline access**: After an online load and completed sync, cached pages are available without a network connection. Edits are stored locally and reconciled when you reconnect. Documents are fetched on demand unless you enable document caching in [[Sync#Configuration]].
* **App-like experience**: Install SilverBullet as a standalone app on your device — it gets its own window, icon, and feels like a native application.
* **Instant loading**: Since your content is synced to your browser’s local storage, cached pages can load without fetching their content from the Server.

--- [vault:corpus/docs/PWA.md] ---
### How offline works

# How offline works
SilverBullet’s [[Sync]] engine keeps configured space content in the browser’s IndexedDB. Pages are synchronized by default. Documents and ignored paths have different rules. When online, changes are continuously synced between the browser and the server. When offline, you work against the local copy. On reconnection, the sync engine reconciles any changes.

A service worker caches the application code itself, so even the SilverBullet UI loads without a network connection.

See also: [[Sync]], [[Collaboration]] (what happens to your offline edits when you reconnect), [[Architecture]]

--- [vault:corpus/docs/Sync.md] ---
### Untitled

SilverBullet is designed as an [[ADR/001 Offline-First PWA|Offline-First]] mindset — that is: your content should be available to you, whether you have an Internet connection or not.

Depending on the edition of SilverBullet that you use, Sync functions slightly differently. When you use the **Server** directly via the browser, your content will be synced to your browser’s local storage (IndexedDB). After an online load and initial sync, cached pages can be read and edited without a connection. Edits reconcile when the Server is reachable again. Documents have separate caching settings below.

[[Desktop]] spaces can _optionally_ be configured with [[Desktop Sync]].

Regardless of the client, sync happens in near-real time when connected. Saves are throttled to about 2 seconds, after which the page is saved and synced immediately.

In the browser, Sync runs in a service worker and therefore only runs when the service worker is active. The service worker is automatically kept active for as long as you have a SilverBullet tab or window open. Some browsers slow web apps down when they are in the background or not in an active tab. This may also affect whether sync happens in the background. Most browsers (including mobile ones), keep service workers running for a little while (perhaps up to a minute), even when e.g. the screen is locked, or another app is activated.

--- [vault:corpus/docs/ADR/007 Core Application Logic on the Client.md] ---
### Decision

# Decision
v2 **eliminates the server-side PlugOS runtime**: plug execution, indexing, the query engine, [[Space Lua]], page rendering, and the [[Sync|sync engine]] now run **only in the client**. In effect, **sync mode becomes the only mode**, and the **server is reduced to a file store** — it lists, reads, writes and deletes files, handles authentication, serves the static client, and runs shell commands. See [[Architecture]].
